ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every director, officer, shareholder and UBO against FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) records, domestic/foreign PEP categories under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and terrorism financing provisions of the Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46. Screening must be completed within 90 days before the incorporation filing and refreshed at least every 12 months or upon any material change in control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Nom d'entreprise et reservation de nom (online portal at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal NUANS name search through Corporations Canada where a federal CBCA name clearance is also required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the enterprise name must include an approved French version; the name may be in French alone or in French with another language, and where a non-French name is used, the French version must appear with it in a non-subordinate manner. Non-Latin scripts require a standardized transliteration into Latin script plus the French legal form designation (e.g., 'Societe par actions' or 'Inc.'). All business names must be consistent with Quebec's linguistic rules for signs, catalogs, invoices, and commercial documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire rejects the proposed name, the applicant will receive a written refusal citing the relevant registry provisions. Within 30 days from the date of the refusal, the applicant may file a reasoned request for reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, optionally accompanied by a revised name or a supporting trademark/charter document. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for judicial review under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01, within the applicable 30-day judicial review period. No statutory extension is available for a valid name reservation; after 90 days the applicant must submit a fresh name reservation application if incorporation has not yet been completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted only if it is a genuine physical address in Quebec, staffed during normal business hours and capable of receiving and forwarding legal process and notices. A post-office box or a pure mail-forwarding virtual address is not acceptable as the company's registered office. For a low-risk creator-MCN agency without a leased storefront, a professional registered agent office in Quebec is commercially permissible as the registered office address, but the company must still maintain books and records accessible to Revenu Quebec at an address in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5-10% for a low-risk, non-licensed digital creator agency in its first fiscal year. The likelihood increases to 15-20% once the business files GST/QST returns and if Revenu Quebec or the Canada Revenue Agency selects the file for a tax audit or compliance verification. Unannounced physical on-site inspections at the registered office are rare but can occur where books and records are kept at a non-compliant virtual address or where payroll/supplier records indicate potential unreported revenue.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1, ss. 3, 28-32, 42, 43, 94, 102 and 122; federal alternative, Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-19, with extra-provincial registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, C.Q.L.R. c. P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Enterprise Registry Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Articles de constitution) filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; shares are issued for the consideration fixed by the board, payable in money, property or past services, and paid-up capital must be supported by a board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of [●] Inc. under the Quebec Business Corporations Act is approved and ratified; that the subscribed shares of the corporation are issued to the subscribing incorporator at the consideration per share set by the board; that the registered office is established at [address], Province of Quebec, and the registered office register is adopted; that [Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; that the board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts at [bank], the execution of all documents, and the appointment of signing officers; and that the corporation’s by-laws and minute book are adopted. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the REQ enterprise registry, confirm compatibility with the Charter of the French Language, and reserve the proposed name for 90 days if desired. The proposed name must include a legal element (Inc., Corp. or Société par actions) and must not cause confusion with an existing enterprise.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or non-compliant, submit a new name for a fresh search and pay the revised reservation fee; REQ normally lifts the objection once a distinguishable name is certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Constitutive Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed articles of incorporation electronically through REQ or by paper if notarized, pay the statutory filing fee, and include the share structure, director count, restrictions on share transfers if any, registered office address, and incorporator declaration. REQ issues the certificate of constitution upon registration.
required_dossiers: Electronic submission confirmation or notarized paper form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is rejected for omissions or inconsistency, correct the articles and re-file; a certificate of non-constitution or notice of defect may be cured by filing a rectified declaration without restarting the legal person’s contemplated existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Number and Legal Publicity Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) automatically issued after constitution, confirm the legal publicity declaration, and update the registered office and director information in the enterprise register. If organized federally, file the extra-provincial registration declaration under the Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Business activity declaration with ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any error in the NEQ record is cured by filing an online updating declaration; administrative corrections are available without penalty if made promptly after discovery.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Organization, By-laws, First Board Resolution and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organization meeting (or pass a written resolution), adopt by-laws, accept the share subscription, issue share certificates, appoint the President, Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, designate the registered office, and define bank signing authorities. Record all resolutions in the minute book and issue the share register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the organization or records are cured by a subsequent unanimous or director resolution ratifying the prior action; statutory books can be regularized retroactively if no prejudice is shown.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Quebec Tax Registrations and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the federal business number (BN) with CRA for corporate income tax, GST/HST and payroll, then activate Quebec accounts with Revenu Québec for corporate income tax, QST, employer deductions and CNESST registration. Present the certificate and board resolution to open the corporate bank account and complete TikTok and Wise B2B payout onboarding.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or business address proof
Bank account and TikTok/Wise onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec returns a query, reconcile the legal publicity declaration, amend the REQ record, and resubmit through the online business account; late registration penalties may be canceled on proof of contemporaneous filings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over digital creator-agency operations under ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating, manufacturing or MCN sectoral permit is required for creator incubation, talent representation or TikTok content-management services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office and studio use does not trigger an authorization under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (C.Q.L.R. c. Q-2); no full EIA report, attestation or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to non-industrial operations; any sanitary discharge must meet municipal wastewater bylaws, and office HVAC systems must comply with the applicable Quebec building ventilation and indoor-air-quality standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the municipal occupancy and fire-safety certificate under the Quebec Building Act and Fire Safety Code, register as an employer with CNESST, and secure a structural load clearance from the landlord for any leased office or studio before operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST, payroll and Part I corporate income tax; portal: CRA 'My Business Account' (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency). Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), Quebec corporate income tax (CO-17) and employer remittances; portal: Revenu Québec 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' (www.revenuquebec.ca). The two authorities coordinate under the Canada–Québec Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement and the GST/HST–QST joint remittance window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Quebec business corporation registers through the CRA 'Business Registration Online' (BRO) one-window service, obtaining a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) with program accounts 'RC' (federal corporate income tax), 'RT' (GST/HST) and 'RP' (payroll), plus a provincial Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) issued by the Registraire des entreprises; Revenu Québec then assigns the QST program account under the collection agreement. Non-resident corporations file Form RC1/RC4312 with the CRA to establish carrying-on-business nexus before the program accounts are activated, and the QST account remains subject to Revenu Québec's separate audit jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' election; a business corporation is invariably a taxable Canadian corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Relevant elections include: (i) fiscal-period election under Income Tax Act s. 249.1; (ii) GST/HST and QST 'Quick Method' elections for qualifying small suppliers (Form GST74 / Revenu Québec VD-505); (iii) ETA s. 267 election among closely related corporations to treat intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration; (iv) going-concern sale election under ETA s. 167 and QST Act s. 202 to zero-rate a transfer of a business universality; (v) hybrid-mismatch integrity rules (Income Tax Act ss. 12.8, 17.3, 21.2, 27.3, 59.4, 63.5, enacted by Bill C-59 in 2024) operate automatically to deny deductions on cross-border hybrid instruments—no election can opt out of those rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Excise Tax Act, Part IX, 5% federal) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ, Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, 9.975% nominal applied on the GST-inclusive price) — a dual VAT system administered federally by the CRA and provincially by Revenu Québec under a joint registration and single-return arrangement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: GST/HST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in four consecutive calendar quarters; the identical CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold applies for QST with Revenu Québec. The foreign-owned Quebec MCN corporation cannot rely on the small-supplier exemption because its global TikTok management, representation and advertising revenue is projected to exceed CAD 30,000 immediately at inception.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital-stamping mandate at the federal level; the CRA accepts electronic invoices (XML, EDIFACT, PDF) and requires invoices to disclose the BN and GST/HST registration number. In Quebec, a business that records its sales electronically in Québec must use a Revenu Québec-certified Sales Recording Module (SRM) for point-of-sale software, with administrative penalties for uncertified systems; Revenu Québec's CLIC portal offers web-service APIs for account administration and QST filings, but there is no government pre-clearance or API stamping of invoices for typical B2B MCN service supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Creator-management, talent-representation and monetization services supplied by the registered Quebec corporation to non-resident TikTok creators qualify for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act and the mirror provision of the QST Act when the recipient is a non-resident at the time the service is performed and the service is not performed in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property; the supplier retains full input-tax credit recovery while charging 0%, but bears the burden of contemporaneous proof of the recipient's non-resident status, offshore place of benefit/use, and payment inflows from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — CBSA Form B13A / Canada Export Reporting System report (where bundled creator merchandise is physically exported)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or CBSA cargo-control document evidencing physical export and foreign destination
Commercial invoice and tax invoice stating 'zero-rated export supply — ETA Schedule VI, Part V' with BN and QST registration numbers
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 or MT950 statement evidencing FX repatriation of TikTok creator settlement proceeds to Canada
Executed MCN service agreement establishing the non-resident creator as recipient, the offshore place of benefit/use, and the service description for audit trail
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On disallowance of zero-rating, the CRA and Revenu Québec reassess the full 5% GST plus 9.975% QST as unremitted net tax, with compound statutory interest running from the original return due date; the gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285.1 is the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax, and directors and officers are personally liable for unremitted GST/QST trust amounts under ETA s. 323 and QST Act s. 432. False customs export statements attract CBSA administrative monetary penalties and possible evasion surcharges of up to 200% of the value of the released goods; the normal 4-year reassessment window is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation, wilful default, or fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Department of Finance Canada, and FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada). The Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) supervises deposit-taking institutions and derivatives dealing in Quebec.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating currency with complete capital and current account convertibility under the Currency Act and the dismantled Foreign Exchange Control Act (repealed 1951). No exchange control approval is required for inbound equity injections, dividend remittances, or trade-related payments. Profit repatriation from a Quebec business corporation is unrestricted; however, dividends and deemed royalties paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25%, reducible under applicable tax treaties), and cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to the Canada Revenue Agency on Form RC599 or through FINTRAC large-transaction filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements in Canada. Export and service receipts, including USD-denominated TikTok creator settlements and MCN commission income, may be fully retained in domestic or foreign-currency bank accounts. Entities holding foreign property (including foreign bank balances, receivables, or shares of non-resident affiliates) with a cost amount exceeding CAD 100,000 must file Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement). All foreign-held revenue is freely convertible to CAD at prevailing market rates via an authorized Canadian dealer (Schedule I bank or registered MSB).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Desjardins Group (Groupe Desjardins - Mouvement des caisses Desjardins)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM — legally viable only as a secondary payment-clearing rail, not as the primary banking relationship. Wise (Wise Payments Canada / Wise B2B) operates in Canada as a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business (MSB), not a bank, and therefore cannot hold statutory escrow deposits, offer CDIC-insured deposits, or provide lending. Offshore EMIs (e.g., EU-licensed digital banks or e-money institutions without Canadian MSB registration) face severe regulatory friction and are generally NOT viable for a Quebec-incorporated operating entity because they cannot clear in CAD through Lynx or the Canadian retail payment system. Recommended structure: primary relationship at a Schedule I chartered bank or Quebec credit union; Wise B2B used exclusively for low-value cross-border creator micro-payouts and multi-currency receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) may generally complete fully remote/video-based KYC onboarding at RBC, TD, BMO, NBC, and Desjardins. However, Quebec-based institutions (National Bank, Desjardins) frequently require an in-branch appointment, a French-language service agreement, or notarized identity attestation. Non-resident directors and UBOs of a Global TikTok MCN Agency must typically attend at least one physical interview at a Canadian branch or with an international private-banking officer; alternatively, a certified true copy of the passport, apostilled corporate documents, and a 120-day source-of-funds statement from the UBO's home-jurisdiction bank may satisfy enhanced due diligence. All beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the corporation must be disclosed and screened against OFAC/OSFI sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding with non-resident directors and beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified and apostilled passports of all directors/UBOs; 120-day source-of-wealth bank statements from the home-bank account; corporate extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; certificate of good standing; business history with prior broker or formation agent records; signed AML attestation and personal net-worth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Many-to-one-to-many creator payout structure causing high transaction velocity and small-ticket cross-border wires
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Creator KYC Portfolio: signed talent representation agreements for each creator, platform payout statements from TikTok, standardized payment instructions (bank/IBAN), batch-payout ledger with transaction narrative, internal AML risk-rating methodology, and transaction-monitoring thresholds documented in the corporate AML/CFT policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for inbound capital injection, including Quebec EPC (Entrepreneur Program) escrow deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement executed with the Quebec financial institution, sworn source-of-funds declaration from the contributing shareholder, share-subscription agreement, bank statement evidencing the originating foreign account, and a copy of the Quebec immigration/EPC undertaking; all documents notarized and translated into English/French.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party platform settlement risk: funds routed through TikTok / ByteDance affiliates, Wise, or intermediary payment aggregators in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed TikTok MCN Agency Agreement, platform settlement statement showing gross commissions and deductions, dashboard export evidencing creator-tagging and revenue share, intercompany services agreement with the foreign parent or affiliate, and a jurisdictional risk matrix demonstrating sanctions screening clearance of all counterparty jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from a foreign shareholder must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank transfers) to the corporation's CAD or USD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank or Desjardins caisses. The transfer narrative should specify 'Capital Contribution to Business Corporation' or 'Equity Subscription under Share Subscription Agreement'. Under FINTRAC, the receiving institution must file a Large Virtual Currency Transaction Report or Large Cash/EFT Transaction Report for amounts at or above CAD 10,000, and the CRA requires Form RC599 for cross-border currency or monetary instruments exceeding CAD 10,000 when physically transported; for electronic transfers, the bank's reporting obligation suffices. Supporting verification: signed share-subscription resolution, certificate of incorporation, Quebec EPC escrow deposit instructions (if applicable), and a source-of-wealth letter. No Bank of Canada approval is required; witholding tax for dividends on the injected capital begins only upon actual distribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for creator compensation and MCN operating disbursements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for single high-value creator settlements and licensing fees; (2) Canada's high-value payment system 'Lynx' for CAD-denominated domestic transactions above CAD 100,000; (3) Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR) for low-value instant CAD payments where deployed; (4) Wise Business API (FINTRAC-registered MSB) for recurring cross-border micro-payouts to creators in multiple jurisdictions; (5) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) only where a supplier of production or advertising services requires documentary credit support — uncommon for MCN agency services and generally not recommended due to documentation cost. Batch disbursements should be submitted with standardized remittance advice referencing the relevant creator agreement to preserve the audit trail for AML review. For payments to U.S. creators, ACH and wire via a U.S. clearing partner are permissible to avoid FX conversion slippage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CAD outright forward contracts (deliverable) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or registered investment dealer, under standard ISDA or Canadian FX master agreement
USD/CAD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible but unnecessary and rarely priced for CAD given CAD's full deliverability
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps, permissible under the AMF/OSFI derivatives framework with central clearing or bilateral margin rules applicable to non-financial counterparties at applicable thresholds
USD/CAD plain-vanilla currency options (European-style), permissible for hedging USD-denominated TikTok commission revenue against CAD operating expense exposure
Natural hedging instruments: USD operating account netting and periodic conversion sweeps at the prevailing spot rate to offset CAD payroll and Quebec tax obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (anniversary rule, not fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No per-month monetary penalty, but the corporation remains in default; after two consecutive years of non-filing, Corporations Canada may issue a 30-day notice and administratively dissolve the corporation; directors risk summary conviction liability for failure to maintain corporate status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation or registration in Quebec (anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty equal to 100% of the annual fee (CAD$118.24) plus interest; failure to file for two consecutive years allows the Registraire to strike the enterprise from the register, resulting in administrative dissolution and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end: file by June 30); balance of tax due 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations claiming the small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; compound daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate on unpaid balances; enforcement by demand and possible director liability for unremitted withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CO-17 Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end: file by June 30); balance of Quebec tax due 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible small and medium-sized corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; prescribed interest compounded daily; risk of garnishment and certificate of lien filed before the Superior Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (GST/HST Return and Net Tax Calculation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end when registered on an annual filing basis (standard for small MCN agency revenue below monthly filer thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compounded prescribed interest; repeated defaults may force mandatory monthly filing and a compliance audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual QST filers; remittance due on the same annual schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid QST plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compounded interest; provincial enforcement by seizure of property and administrative register sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory audit for a private CBCA or QBCA corporation. An audit is compulsory if the corporation is a reporting issuer (publicly traded or publicly distributed securities), if a shareholder holding at least 5% of the voting shares (CBCA) or the statutory minority under the QBCA demands one, or if a sectoral regulator (e.g., AMF authorization for securities activity) requires audited financial statements. A closely held TikTok MCN agency may permanently eliminate the audit burden by unanimous or special shareholder resolution, provided no objecting shareholder exists.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS as issued by the IASB for reporting issuers and certain large enterprises; private corporations may elect Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II). Financial statements prepared under either framework are accepted by CRA and Revenu Québec for T2 and CO-17 filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Quebec's transparency rules administered by the Registraire des entreprises, the annual declaration must confirm and update each ultimate beneficiary holding 25% or more of voting rights or value; any share transfer affecting this control must be stated in the annual declaration. Independently, a CBCA corporation must maintain an on-site Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC register), updated within 15 days of any change in significant control, although this register is not separately filed with Corporations Canada. Tax-level ownership details are also reflected in the T2, CO-17, and Canadian securities information returns.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing by-laws, resolutions, and share transfer records
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC register — CBCA requirement)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$200–US$650 per year (CAD$275–CAD$900) for a Quebec head office address, registered agent, and statutory records custody
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,200–US$10,800 per year (CAD$4,500–CAD$15,000) for a compact private MCN agency when a full audit is demanded; US$0 if shareholders elect the private-company audit exemption

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal (general corporate) + 11.5% Quebec provincial = 26.5% combined headline rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC: federal rate 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income (small business deduction); Quebec SMB rate 3.2% on first CAD 500,000; combined statutory SME rate ≈ 12.2% before refundable credits; SR&ED ITC (35% refundable for CCPCs on qualifying expenditures); Quebec refundable tax credits for multimedia/video game productions and other innovation incentives.
